transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I suppose I came because I just can’t seem to get things in order anymore. I know that probably sounds small, but my kitchen table is just covered with papers—my husband’s appointment things, church flyers, notes from the senior center, little lists I started and didn’t finish. And I sit down meaning to sort it out, but then I can’t decide what to do first, and somehow the whole day is gone. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but it’s been getting hard for me.
Have you ever experienced a time before this where you felt similarly overwhelmed or down for a period of time?

I’m not sure I’d say “down,” exactly… not in the way people sometimes mean it, I don’t think. Overwhelmed, maybe, here and there over the years, but I can’t really point to a clear period like that. I’ve usually just tried to push through things and not make too much of it.

Is that the sort of thing you’re asking?
Have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless most of the time lately?

I don’t think so… not most of the time. I mean, I get frustrated with myself, and sometimes I feel a little discouraged when I can’t keep up, but I wouldn’t say I’m hopeless or sad all day. Is that what you’re asking?
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things as much as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you usually find pleasurable?

I don’t think I’ve lost interest, no… at least not in any big way. I still like the things I’ve always liked when I actually get myself to them. Maybe I don’t do as much as I used to, but I wouldn’t say the pleasure is gone. Does that make sense?
Have you been feeling more tired or low on energy lately, even if you haven’t been doing much?

I don’t think so, not especially. I mean, I’m 70, so I suppose I don’t have the same energy I used to, but I haven’t noticed some big change where I feel exhausted for no reason. At least, I don’t think so. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, feeling restless or fidgety lately?

Not slower, I don’t think. If anything… I do get a little fidgety, though I try not to. Like if I’m sitting in a meeting and trying to be polite, I’ll realize I’m rubbing my hands or tapping my foot, or clicking a pen without thinking. Sometimes I shift around enough that someone looks over, which is embarrassing. It’s not on purpose… is that the kind of restlessness you mean?
Over the past few weeks or months, would you say that your frustration or discouragement has become a near daily experience, affecting your ability to get things done or enjoy your day?

I’m not sure I’d say near daily, no. I mean, I do get frustrated with myself sometimes when things don’t go smoothly, but I try not to dwell on it. I wouldn’t want to make it sound worse than it is. It doesn’t feel like I’m discouraged all day or that it’s ruining my day, if that makes sense.
Have you found it harder lately to focus on things, like following a conversation, reading, or making decisions?

Yes… I suppose I have noticed that some. I don’t want to overstate it, but if there’s a television on in the next room, or if a couple of people start talking near me at the senior center, my mind just sort of goes with that instead. Then I’ll look back at what I was writing or trying to plan, and I’ve lost my place.

It’s a little embarrassing, because it sounds so simple, but yes, that kind of focus has been harder. Is that what you mean?
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to think clearly, make decisions, or remember things lately?

A little, yes… though I don’t know if I’d call it “not thinking clearly” exactly. It’s more that things slip past me.

I’ve missed returning calls, and I’ll leave a bill sitting under a stack of mail and only notice later. I’ve forgotten errands I told my daughter I’d take care of. And more than once I realized too late that I never confirmed one of my husband’s appointments, which makes me feel awful.

I try to write things down, but… yes, lately it has been happening more than I’d like to admit. Is that the kind of memory thing you’re asking about?
Have you had any period in the last few months where you felt down or discouraged nearly every day for two weeks or more, even if it has improved by now?

I don’t think so… not for two weeks straight like that. I’ve had low days, of course, and I can get discouraged with myself, but it tends to come and go. I wouldn’t want to say it was nearly every day unless I was really sure, and I don’t think that’s been the case.
Have you ever had a period in your life when you felt down or lost interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?

I’m not sure… I don’t think I’ve had anything like that for two weeks in a row, at least not that I would confidently call it that. I’ve had sad stretches, and times where I didn’t feel much like doing things, but I’m not sure it was most of the day, nearly every day.

I don’t want to answer wrong. I’d say no, not that I can clearly remember.
Have you ever had a period in your life when you felt down or lost interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?

I think my answer is still… no, not that I can clearly remember. I mean, I’ve certainly had unhappy times, and times I didn’t feel very interested in much, but I don’t think it was most of the day every day for two full weeks.

I hope that’s the kind of answer you mean. I just don’t want to overstate it.
Over the past year, have there been any times when you felt down, sad, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?

Over the past year… I don’t think so, no. I’ve had times where I felt discouraged or kind of low, but I can’t say it was most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks straight.

I hope that’s okay—I just don’t want to make it sound more serious than it was.
Have you noticed that you don’t take as much pleasure in things you used to enjoy, or that you’ve lost interest in doing them altogether?

I don’t think I’ve lost interest altogether, no. I still enjoy things when I actually do them. Sometimes I’m slower to get started, or I don’t think to do them, but I wouldn’t say the pleasure is gone.

Does that answer it the right way?
Over the past two weeks, have you had days where you felt down, sad, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, or where you lost interest in most things you usually enjoy?

In the past two weeks… no, I don’t think so. I’ve had a few blah days, I guess, but not where I was sad or hopeless most of the day nearly every day. And I haven’t really lost interest in most things—if anything, I just don’t always get around to them.

I hope that’s clear enough.
In the past two weeks, have you had little interest or pleasure in doing things most of the day, nearly every day, or felt down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?

I think… no, not most of the day nearly every day. I’ve had moments where I feel kind of flat or unmotivated, but I wouldn’t call it depressed or hopeless. And I do still get pleasure from things when I’m doing them.

I hope I’m answering that clearly.

In the past two weeks, have you had days when you felt down, depressed, or hopeless for most of the day, nearly every day, or when you had little interest or pleasure in doing things for most of the day, nearly every day?

I’m not really sure I can say that I have, no. I mean, I have some slower or low-energy days, but not where I’d describe myself as down or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day. And I still do enjoy things once I get myself into them. Does that make sense?
Have you ever had a period in your life when you felt down or lost interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?

I’m not sure… I don’t really think so, at least not in a clear way like that. I’ve had hard patches in life, of course, but I don’t remember a time where I was down or uninterested in things most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks straight.

I hope that answers what you’re asking.
In the past two weeks, have you had any days where you felt down or had little interest in doing things for most of the day, even if it was just for a few days?

Maybe a day here or there where I felt kind of blah or didn’t feel like starting anything, but not really most of the day, I don’t think. Once I get going, I usually can enjoy things. So… no, I wouldn’t say I’ve had days like that in the way you mean. Is that okay?
Have you felt that your ability to think clearly, concentrate, or make decisions has been noticeably worse most days, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Yes… I think so, though I don’t know if I’d say it’s “thinking clearly” exactly. It’s more that I get pulled off track very easily. Like if the television is on in the next room, or two people start talking near me at the senior center, my mind just goes right over to that, and then I lose my place in what I was writing or what I was trying to plan.

It does happen a lot, most days, I guess. I don’t mean to make it sound dramatic, but it’s noticeable. Is that the kind of concentration trouble you mean?
